transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-13 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen, Carlos Ortega (Redwood); Lena Patel, Raj Malhotra, Olivia Zhang (AcmeCorp)

Summary: quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking, walked through SDK calls, Console view, and Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization. Discussed VPC/on-prem concerns and SOC2/KMS encryption.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're excited to show a quick walkthrough of Redwood's hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints, I'm Maya, AE on the account. Carlos is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Lena Patel: Hi, thanks — excited. Quick context, we run Acme search for ecommerce, around 5M queries/day, currently using Elastic search plus custom TF-IDF and some heuristic reranking. Latency is a big thing for us.
[00:26] Carlos Ortega: Great. I'll jump into the demo, we'll show an end-to-end: embedding generation, vector retrieval against your vector DB, then a Redwood hosted reranker endpoint that re-scores top-k for final relevance.
[00:40] Raj Malhotra: Quick Q up front — do you recommend hosted + our vector DB or do you store vectors in Redwood? We're trying to avoid vendor lock in.
[00:51] Carlos Ortega: Totally — our hosted API works with any external vector store. You can continue using OpenSearch or Pinecone or Milvus. We also provide optional managed vector storage if customers want it, but it's pluggable.
[01:04] Olivia Zhang: Do you re-run embeddings at query time or precompute? We have both user queries and product updates so mix.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Common pattern: precompute item embeddings and store them; query embeddings are computed at runtime. For freshness you can re-embed updates; our Console has a 'reindex' job helper.
[01:24] Carlos Ortega: (screenshare) Ok here's the SDK call: embed = client.embeddings.create({ model: "rw-embed-large-1", input: query }) then vector DB query, then rerank = client.rerank.create({ model: "rw-rerank-1", candidates: topK }) — note those are pseudocode lines.
[01:43] Lena Patel: Are those model names public? we saw a doc that mentioned Redwood-verified models, just want to confirm naming.
[01:52] Maya Chen: Yes, we maintain curated models and variants; for hosted we surface performance profiles in the catalog. Some customers pin versions for consistent results.
[02:05] Raj Malhotra: Latency — can you give ballpark for 95th pct for embed + topK rerank? We're targeting <300ms for UI.
[02:14] Carlos Ortega: For a hosted flow with rw-embed-large and rw-rerank-1 and topK=10, we've seen median ~80-120ms and 95th around 180-260ms depending on network and vector DB roundtrip. If you need <200ms consistently we recommend routing in-region and enabling our prefix/KV cache for frequent queries.
[02:33] Olivia Zhang: Cache — we have lots of repeat queries, how does KV cache handle query variants?
[02:40] Carlos Ortega: Prefix/KV cache is mostly helpful for conversational long inputs; for search typically we cache popular query embeddings and the reranker results if allowed by your retention policy. Cache policies are configurable — you can set TTLs per route.
[02:54] Lena Patel: Security — we operate in EU, need data residency, SOC 2, SSO, and KMS integration. Can hosted meet that?
[03:03] Maya Chen: Yes — hosted in our EU region supports data residency. We're SOC 2 Type II, support SAML SSO and RBAC, and integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest for Dedicated/Private; hosted offers encryption but for BYOK KMS you'd look at Dedicated or Private plans. We'll send our security pack.
[03:21] Raj Malhotra: So for pilot we probably need to run a benchmark, do you help with that?
[03:26] Carlos Ortega: Absolutely — we can run a bench using your sample dataset. We'll provide a simple harness (python script) that hits the embeddings + reranker endpoints and records latencies and P95, also includes an evaluation harness for relevance metrics (MRR/NDCG) if you provide labeled judgments or click logs.
[03:44] Maya Chen: I'll include that in the pilot scope.
[03:47] Lena Patel: On cost — how do you price the reranking part vs embeddings? We currently look at per-token and compute.
[03:54] Maya Chen: Hosted pricing: embeddings per embedding unit, rerank is per-call + per-token where applicable. For rerank we often have a pricing band based on topK. For large volume we recommend batching or a partial rerank approach — e.g., lightweight lexical filter, then embed+rerank top200->top10. We can show Optimize suggestions to reduce unit cost.
[04:18] Raj Malhotra: Batching — if we batch 8 queries at once what happens to latency?
[04:23] Carlos Ortega: Batching helps throughput, but increases tail latency. Optimize will recommend batching sizes based on your latency SLO. For UI you generally keep small batches or no batching. For async backfill you can be aggressive.
[04:36] Olivia Zhang: Can the reranker access product metadata fields? e.g., boosting by availability or price?
[04:43] Carlos Ortega: Yes, reranker can take structured fields as features; you can pass metadata in the candidate objects and our model can be prompted to account for them or you can use a hybrid feature scoring.
[04:55] [screen: Console] Carlos Ortega: Here is the Console route config — you can set model, topK, rerank threshold, TTLs, and a fallback policy that routes to a cheaper model if capacity constrained. You can also toggle quantization profiles per model to reduce cost.
[05:12] Lena Patel: Quantization — how aggressive? does it hurt quality?
[05:16] Carlos Ortega: We suggest 8-bit quant for many rerank models; our Optimize tool will run A/B tests on a small prompt set and report quality regressions. Usually quality impact is small for reranking, but we do surface regression alerts.
[05:32] Raj Malhotra: Any concerns about vendor lock-in for model variants?
[05:36] Maya Chen: We try to be model-agnostic; you can switch models and pin versions. If you host vectors in your vector DB there's minimal lock-in.
[05:45] Olivia Zhang: Workflow question — for evaluation, we have click logs. How do you recommend we compute relevance metrics?
[05:52] Carlos Ortega: If you can provide click logs we can derive implicit relevance labels and compute MRR/NDCG; if you have judge-labeled pairs even better. We'll include an eval harness in the bench kit.
[06:05] Lena Patel: Let's see an example rerank result — show us before/after.
[06:10] Carlos Ortega: (demo) Here's query: "red running shoes size 10" — lexical results rank a mismatch; after embeddings + rerank topK=10 the correct product with 'size 10' visible rises to top 3.
[06:25] [mild crosstalk] Olivia Zhang: Hmm, wow that ordering looks reasonable but need A/B test.
[06:31] Carlos Ortega: We'll instrument the console to log per-route token/cost breakdown — helps you see per-query cost.
[06:40] Raj Malhotra: Network — if we keep vectors in our VPC, how does hosted rerank call the vector DB?
[06:46] Carlos Ortega: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink style connectivity for Dedicated and Private customers. For pure hosted there's an option to open a secure tunnel or use an API gateway — we can detail network options in the security doc.
[06:59] Lena Patel: Any customers running this in EU with strict residency?
[07:03] Maya Chen: Yes, several enterprise customers, we'll share a case study.
[07:08] Olivia Zhang: For the pilot, what's a typical dataset size? We can share a subset.
[07:13] Maya Chen: For initial bench 100k items + a month of queries is common. For quicker checks 10k items + 10k queries helps.
[07:22] Lena Patel: Ok let's talk timeline: we need legal review too.
[07:25] Maya Chen: Understood — we'll send the security pack and the standard MSA; legal review usually takes 2-4 weeks depending. For pilot we can run without a full contract under a trial pilot NDA — we'll follow up.
[07:39] [00:07:40] Carlos Ortega: (shows sample python harness) This script creates embeddings in batch of 64, queries top_k then hits rerank endpoint for each candidate set, records latency and logs scores. It also outputs an evaluation CSV for NDCG.
[08:05] Olivia Zhang: A few transcribed words here are odd, but looks straightforward. Will you provide the sample script?
[08:10] Carlos Ortega: Yes — we'll put it in the pilot folder on the link I'll share.
[08:15] Raj Malhotra: Any SLA on hosted? For Dedicated we need SLOs.
[08:20] Maya Chen: Hosted has basic uptime commitments; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency and uptime. We'll outline options.
[08:26] Lena Patel: Are there any hidden costs — like per-candidate reformatting?
[08:31] Maya Chen: No hidden charges, rerank cost accounts for the candidate scoring and tokens. We'll provide a cost estimate based on your topK distribution.
[08:40] [pause]
[08:45] Maya Chen: Ok, quick recap — next steps: we'll send pricing + pilot scope, Carlos will prepare benchmark harness, Acme to share sample data, and schedule SE-led bench week of 2027-07-26. Anything to add?
[08:58] Lena Patel: Please include our legal contact (I've cc'd in calendar) in the security pack.
[09:03] Olivia Zhang: Also include an example of the rerank input format.
[09:07] Maya Chen: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[09:10] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (rw-embed referenced as "our embed"), speaker overlaps, and some product names slightly altered.
